title: SLO-anchored Canary Abort Advisor and Tuning Playbook
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Build an advisor service and operational playbook that automatically recommends and optionally enforces rollback/evacuation actions for model rollouts (canaries, A/B tests, shadow traffic) using composite SLO signals: latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput. The goal is to reduce MTTR for bad rollouts while minimizing unnecessary rollbacks through statistically principled threshold tuning and cohort-aware baselining.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor can compute an evacuation score from live telemetry and historical baselines for a canary cohort in < 30s
Actionable recommendations appear in Console canary UI and via webhook/alert (scale: warn/partial-evacuate/full-rollback)
Auto-rollback policy executes sandboxed rollback action with auditable event and allows manual override within 2 minutes
False positive rate (unnecessary full-rollback) under internal test workload < 5% across 50+ simulated canaries
Advisor produces tunable threshold suggestions (absolute floors + relative-change bands) derived from traffic-aware statistical model and shows confidence bands
design_decisions: Use hybrid thresholds: absolute floors for safety (eg. latency > 2000ms) + relative change windows (eg. >20% degrade vs cohort baseline)
Signal fusion via weighted scoring rather than brittle AND/OR rules so partial degradations (token cost + throughput) can trigger graduated actions
Prioritize cohort-aware baselines: compare canary to matched cohort (same region, request size distribution) to avoid spurious alerts from traffic shifts
Adopt a conservative default for A/B tests: require higher statistical confidence before auto-rollback; allow advisory recommendations sooner
Run shadow traffic analysis asynchronously (no live rollback) but surface divergence metrics and rollback score in Console
tradeoffs: Complex statistical models reduce false positives but increase compute/latency for scoring; we cap model complexity to meet UI latency budget
Aggressive auto-rollback reduces blast radius but increases risk of rollbacks from transient spikes; mitigated by temporal smoothing and minimum confirmation window
Cohort baselining improves signal quality but requires accurate labels for cohorts; fallback to global baseline if cohort insufficient data
Token-cost SLOs are correlated with output length and prompt mix; we normalize by token-per-request distribution to avoid punishing models used for longer generation tasks
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Spike completed for sequential testing approaches (CUSUM, Bayesian online change point) — CUSUM selected for latency/error quick detection, Bayesian for cost drift analysis
2026-02-23: Prototype scoring lambda that reads Prometheus + trace traces and computes per-cohort score deployed to staging (link to demo dashboard)
2026-03-02: Design review with PM & Console team — agreed on 3 outcome tiers: advisory, partial-evacuation, full-rollback; manual override REST endpoint required
2026-03-07: Intern-run simulation across 200 synthetic canaries shows 60% reduction in advisory noise vs baseline thresholding; false-positive full-rollback rate at 7% — needs tuning
2026-03-10: Implemented adjustable weight configs per signal and UI for operators to tune sensitivity per project; preparing canary in prod next week behind feature flag
steps: Implement scoring service that ingests Prometheus histograms and trace-derived latency and error samples
Add cohort classifier to routing layer to attach cohort metadata to canary traces
Expose advisor decision API and webhook for Console and alerting integration
Implement sandboxed rollback executor with audit trail and retry semantics
Add UI in Console: score timeline, top contributing signals, recommended action and confidence
Run extended chaos and synthetic-load experiments, iterate thresholds based on observed FP/FN tradeoff
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Staging-only advisor running in advisory-only mode for 2 weeks
Phase 1: Canary rollouts in low-traffic projects with advisory+operator notifications
Phase 2: Allow partial-evacuation (move 50% of canary traffic to fallback) behind feature flag
Phase 3: Enable auto-rollback for high-confidence matches in select low-risk services
Phase 4: Gradually expand auto-rollback to more services, add per-project sensitivity controls
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring logic with synthetic distributions
Integration tests: end-to-end canary lifecycle (deploy -> score -> action -> rollback) in CI sandbox
Fuzz tests with traffic shape changes and token-length skew
Run canary corpus from past incidents to validate detection and avoid repeat false rollbacks
SLA for scoreboard latency: end-to-end detection + recommendation < 30s in staging
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Auto-rollback during regional infrastructure blips. Mitigation: require cross-region signal confirmation or elevated severity threshold
Risk: High token-cost models flagged due to longer outputs. Mitigation: normalize cost by expected tokens per route and expose opt-outs for known long-gen routes
Risk: Exhausting historical cohort data for new services. Mitigation: fallback to rolling historical window and increase conservative bias
